clue.text: Splash out in an urban setting?

parts.note: the real meaning: spend lavishly, without restraint
the setter's joke: read literally, the idiom describes travelling into a city

explanation.surface: Someone splurging on a shopping trip in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the idiom is being taken literally: heading into a city is, word for word, what the phrase says.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something lavishly or with great enthusiasm, especially spending money freely.

clue.text: To some extent handing over nominal control

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer sits inside their run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of handing, all of over and the start of nominal

explanation.surface: A ruler passing on power that was only ever titular.
explanation.definitionFit: To control a country or organisation is to rule or direct it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: National rising during sound of alarm

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a national of Scotland
during a time is in it

explanation.surface: A national uprising breaking out while warning bells ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National rising' reads as a revolt, but it is a Scot turned upside down in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, historically rung to rouse a town.

clue.text: Flier from the tropics moving north over time

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of north rearranged
bird is slang for time served in prison

explanation.surface: A tropical bird migrating northwards over the seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' puts the first piece above the second. Bird for a prison sentence comes from rhyming slang, bird-lime for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The thornbird is a South American ovenbird that builds huge stick nests, so a tropical flier.

clue.text: Pussy pursues drink in humorous film

indicators.note: one that pursues comes behind, so this piece is placed after the other

parts.note: a spirit, a drink
Pussy Galore is the Bond girl in Goldfinger, so her surname follows Pussy

explanation.surface: A cat chasing after a drink in a comic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussy pursues drink' puts the Pussy piece after the drink. Whisky Galore! is a 1949 Ealing comedy about a shipwrecked cargo of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names an Ealing Studios comedy film, so the answer is an example of a humorous movie.

clue.text: Trendy comedian's success

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
a success, as in a hit record

explanation.surface: A fashionable stand-up enjoying a successful run.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but works as 'has': the comedian has the success after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means being fashionable and up to date, an informal adjective.

clue.text: Picture that's included in periodical? Just the opposite

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits inside it
this phrase swaps the roles just described, so the outer and inner pieces trade places

parts.note: i.e., Latin id est, that is
short for magazine

explanation.surface: Asking whether a photograph appeared in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, that's goes inside the periodical; 'Just the opposite' reverses the roles, so the periodical goes inside that's.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness, a straightforward noun synonym.

clue.text: Bill's place for putting things aside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a billboard where posters, or bills, are put up
second meaning: storing things away for the future

explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a large outdoor advertising board is called this, and the word also means stockpiling supplies.

clue.text: Cross note written about noisy partygoers

indicators.note: something written about another thing goes round it, enclosing it

parts.note: te, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
people at loud dance parties

explanation.surface: An angry note written to complain about rowdy party guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for the note's tone; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross or travel across an area, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Carriage seen in station

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
second meaning: a major London railway terminus

explanation.walkthrough: London Victoria is a main railway station; the victoria carriage was named after the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a low horse-drawn vehicle for two passengers and a major London rail terminus.

clue.text: Fruit always eaten by father

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it

parts.note: an affectionate word for father
ay (aye) is a poetic word for ever, always

explanation.surface: A dad who always eats a particular fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaya is a tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Ariadne's raven loses tail flying in mountains

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order
losing its tail means the bird's final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, with the s
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A mythical heroine's pet raven, missing its tail feathers, flying over a range of peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariadne is the Cretan princess of Greek myth; her name, with its apostrophe s, is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sierra Nevada is a mountain range, found both in Spain and in California.

clue.text: Concede game, ignoring second rule

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: in chess you resign to concede a game
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A player giving up a match while disregarding the second rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second rule' reads as a rule number two; second is the letter removed and rule is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period of their rule; as a verb, to reign is to rule.

clue.text: Feeding frenzy in Kew almost causes a critical situation

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A feeding frenzy among the wildlife at Kew Gardens creating a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: On a knife edge describes a tense, precarious state where the outcome could go either way.

clue.text: Unique digital recordings

parts.note: surface reading: one-off computer files or music tracks
the setter's reading: digital means of the fingers, and the marks they leave are unique to each person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers; here it means relating to digits, the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Police record the marks left by fingertips, and no two people's patterns are identical.

clue.text: Creaky sounds made by parts of house

indicators.note: sounds signals that the words are said out loud, not spelt

parts.note: two parts of a house, said together

explanation.surface: An old house creaking in its various rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic joints are stiff and aching, so a rheumatic person moves in a creaky way.

clue.text: Paddy heading off for cold expanse

indicators.note: with its heading off, the first letter is removed

parts.note: a paddy is a flooded field where rice is grown

explanation.surface: An Irishman setting off across a frozen landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irishman's name; it is the rice paddy.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefield is a large expanse of ice, on land or floating at sea.

clue.text: Passionate priest expressing doubt — he hopes to take you in

definitions.text: he hopes to take you in

parts.note: hot-blooded, ardent
Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible, a crossword favourite
er, a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A fervent priest voicing uncertainty about whether to accept someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take you in' hints at a con man, but it means giving you a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel keeper wants guests to stay, so he hopes to accommodate you.

clue.text: Outlandish word replaces one that has mass appeal

indicators.note: outlandish means strange or bizarre, so the letters take an odd new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange word being substituted for one that's widely popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd-pleaser is a performer or show that is popular with the general public.

clue.text: Boy embracing girl upset sportsman

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one name goes round the other

parts.note: short for Reginald
short for Florence

explanation.surface: A boy hugging an upset girl, with a sportsman nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' seems to describe the girl's mood, but it turns the whole couple upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer is a person who plays golf, so a kind of sportsman.

clue.text: Enthusiast losing mother in maze with many following

indicators.note: what is following comes after, so the second piece is placed at the end
losing something means the letters for it are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
an informal word for mother, removed
a lot, many

explanation.surface: A keen pursuer, abandoning his mother in a maze with a crowd behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatical, uncompromising supporter of a cause, an extreme kind of enthusiast.

clue.text: Note finally gone in setback for poetry

parts.note: F is a musical note

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a reverse is a defeat or setback

indicators.note: finally points at the end of the word, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of gone

explanation.surface: A musical note dropped from a song that disappointed the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Note leads the answer; the last letter of gone sits inside setback after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry without regular metre or rhyme, a form of poetic writing.

clue.text: Hole found in corrupt material

indicators.note: something found in another lies inside it

parts.note: base, morally wicked
O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: A hole discovered in damaged fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Voile is a thin, semi-transparent fabric of cotton or silk used for curtains and dresses.

clue.text: Animal sounds like cow (English)

parts.note: a cow's lowing noises
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A creature whose call resembles that of an English cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' is not an indicator here: it literally means the noises a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large deer of northern forests, a fair example of an animal.

clue.text: Extract content of felicitations

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside it, so the answer is buried within the next word

parts.note: the letters lie inside the word, after its first letter

explanation.surface: Drawing out the gist of a congratulatory message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like a noun, as in a passage, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or obtain a response or information from someone.

clue.text: Constant companion of Christian

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the pilgrim who travels with Christian in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.walkthrough: Christian here is the hero of Bunyan's allegory, not just any believer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means loyal and steadfast, and the same word names Christian's fellow traveller in Bunyan's allegory.

clue.text: Exceedingly mended

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mild euphemism for damned, very
second meaning: repaired by sewing, as socks are

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a description of a careful repair; they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a polite intensifier standing in for damned, and also the past tense of repairing holes with needle and yarn.

clue.text: Pub takes in a very small amount at cards

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: a bar, a drinking place
taken as written
cc, a cubic centimetre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub drinker sipping a tiny amount while playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' looks like a link word joining the card game, but it supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game in which players bet on which hand totals nearer nine.
